user.title: Find Assistant
user.description: Independent of Bermuda -- tracks FMDN, IRK, and static-MAC BLE devices across your ESPHome bluetooth_proxy rooms directly. Click Submit to create it; you'll add devices next, via Configure.

abort.already_configured: Find Assistant is already set up -- use Configure to manage devices.

init.title: Find Assistant
init.description: Choose what to configure. You can come back to this menu any time to add more devices or change settings.

menu_options.sync_google_account: Link/relink a Google Find My account
menu_options.add_static_mac: Add a device by static MAC

import_fmdn.title: Import FMDN devices.json
import_fmdn.description: Upload devices.json (from device_lister/list_devices.py), or paste its contents. This replaces the current FMDN device list.

sync_google_account.title: Link a Google Find My account
sync_google_account.description:
Upload the secrets.json produced by a one-time, external GoogleFindMyTools login (see LICENSE_NOTICE.md), or paste its contents. Replaces your FMDN device list with a live pull from your account and keeps it synced automatically. If sync ever starts failing, redo that login and upload a fresh secrets.json here.

Phones are added automatically as IRK devices where possible. LE Audio devices (headphones/earbuds) can't be tracked by this integration at all -- Google's API doesn't expose a usable key for them, so they're skipped.

sync_google_irk_added.title: Added as IRK devices
sync_google_irk_added.description: Added/updated as IRK devices using their account_key: {names}. This works well for phones, but isn't guaranteed for locator tags -- if one never resolves anything, remove it later via "Remove a device". Submit to continue.

add_irk.title: Add a device by IRK
add_irk.description: For devices using standard Bluetooth address rotation (phones, some earbuds/headphones). Type the IRK with or without separators -- colons, dashes, spaces, or none are all fine.

add_static_mac.title: Add a device by static MAC
add_static_mac.description: For devices that never change their Bluetooth address. Pick from the advertisements currently visible to your proxies (strongest signal first), or type a MAC manually -- colons, dashes, spaces, or no separator are all accepted (AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF, AA BB CC DD EE FF, or AABBCCDDEEFF).

remove_device.title: Remove a device
remove_device.description: Select one or more devices to stop tracking -- listed as "Name (id) -- location, seen ..." (only while the integration is running). This also deletes each one's HA device entry and sensors.

map_proxy_room.title: Override a proxy's room
map_proxy_room.description: Pick a proxy -- it shows its current room, auto-detected from its HA Area or overridden here. Leave the override blank to fall back to the auto-detected room.

remove_proxy_room.title: Remove a proxy room name
remove_proxy_room.description: Select one or more room-name overrides to clear. That proxy then falls back to its automatically-detected Area or device name.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description:
Optional: move each tracked device's Area to match its current proxy (off by default, since it relocates the device as it roams). The sync interval only applies once a Google account is linked -- 0 means manual sync only.

Merging with BSkando's "Google Find My Device" integration (if installed) shares one Device page per tag between both integrations. Note: removing a device here while merged will also remove that integration's tracking of the same tag, since Home Assistant treats them as one Device.

data.google_sync_interval_hours: Hours between automatic Google account resyncs (0 = manual only)
data.merge_googlefindmy_device: Merge devices with BSkando's Google Find My Device integration, if installed

error.no_devices_provided: Upload a file or paste devices.json contents.
error.file_read_failed: Couldn't read the uploaded file. Check Home Assistant's logs for details.
error.invalid_json: That doesn't look like a valid devices.json -- check it's a JSON array of {name, identity_key, pair_date} objects, and that no two entries share the same identity_key. Check Home Assistant's logs for the specific problem.
error.invalid_irk: IRK must be 32 hex characters (16 bytes) -- colons, dashes, and spaces between bytes are fine, e.g. 00:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99:AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF.
error.invalid_mac: MAC must be 6 bytes of hex -- colons, dashes, and spaces between bytes are fine, e.g. AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF.
error.no_devices_selected: Select at least one to remove, or go back if you didn't mean to.
error.no_secrets_provided: Upload a file or paste secrets.json contents.
error.invalid_secrets: That doesn't look like a valid secrets.json -- check it's the file produced by a completed GoogleFindMyTools login (needs fcm_credentials, username, aas_token, and owner_key).
error.sync_failed: Couldn't sync with your Google account: {error}. If this persists, secrets.json may have expired -- redo the GoogleFindMyTools login and re-upload it.

abort.no_proxy_rooms_to_remove: No proxy room names are configured yet.
abort.no_proxies_detected: No Bluetooth proxies are currently online -- make sure at least one is connected, then try again.
abort.sync_failed: Couldn't sync with your Google account: {error}. If this persists, secrets.json may have expired -- redo the GoogleFindMyTools login and re-upload it.

google_sync_failed.title: Google Find My account sync is failing
google_sync_failed.description: The last automatic sync of your linked Google Find My account failed -- check Home Assistant's logs for the specific error. This is often caused by secrets.json expiring (password change, long dormancy, etc.). Redo the GoogleFindMyTools login flow and re-upload a fresh secrets.json via Find Assistant's Configure -> "Link/relink a Google Find My account".
